title: Decimals
description: Understanding decimal place value, comparing and ordering, adding and subtracting decimals, and converting between fractions, decimals and percentages.

notes.heading: Decimal Place Value
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A decimal is a way of writing a number that is not a whole number. The decimal point separates the whole-number part from the fractional part.

🔑 Key Concept
Each digit to the right of the decimal point has a value ten times smaller than the one before it:

$$0.1 = \dfrac{1}{10}, \quad 0.01 = \dfrac{1}{100}, \quad 0.001 = \dfrac{1}{1000}$$

In the number $23.456$:
• $2$ is in the tens place
• $3$ is in the ones place
• $4$ is in the tenths place ($4 \times 0.1$)
• $5$ is in the hundredths place ($5 \times 0.01$)
• $6$ is in the thousandths place ($6 \times 0.001$)

💡 Worked Example
What is the value of the digit $7$ in $9.074$?

Step 1: Locate the digit after the decimal point.
$7$ is the second digit after the point.

Step 2: Name the place value.
Second decimal place = hundredths.

So the value of $7$ is $7$ hundredths, or $\dfrac{7}{100}$ or $0.07$.

⚠️ Common Misconception
The digit furthest to the right is not automatically the smallest value — it depends on its place. In $0.123$, the $3$ is thousandths; in $0.23$, the $3$ is hundredths.

notes.heading: Comparing and Ordering Decimals
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To compare two decimals, we decide which has the larger value by comparing digits in the same place-value columns.

🔑 How it works
1. Line up the decimal points.
2. Add trailing zeros so every number has the same number of decimal places.
3. Compare digits from left to right, starting with the largest place value.

💡 Worked Example
Order these numbers from smallest to largest: $0.6$, $0.58$, $0.605$, $0.061$.

Step 1: Write each number with three decimal places.
$0.6 = 0.600$
$0.58 = 0.580$
$0.605 = 0.605$
$0.061 = 0.061$

Step 2: Compare digit by digit from the left.
$0.061$ has 0 tenths, so it is smallest.
Then $0.580 < 0.600 < 0.605$.

Final order: $0.061,\ 0.58,\ 0.6,\ 0.605$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Thinking more digits always means a bigger number. For example, $0.5 > 0.499$ even though $0.499$ has more digits. Use trailing zeros to compare fairly.

notes.heading: Adding and Subtracting Decimals
notes.body:
🔑 Key Concept
When adding or subtracting decimals, the decimal points must stay in a straight column. If the numbers have different lengths, fill the shorter one with trailing zeros so each column lines up.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Addition
Find $3.75 + 1.8$.

Step 1: Write vertically with decimal points aligned.
$$\begin{array}{r} 3.75 \\ +\ 1.80 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Step 2: Add from right to left.
Hundredths: $5 + 0 = 5$
Tenths: $7 + 8 = 15$ (write $5$, carry $1$)
Ones: $3 + 1 + 1 = 5$

$$3.75 + 1.8 = 5.55$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Subtraction
Find $5.2 - 3.87$.

Step 1: Write vertically with trailing zero.
$$\begin{array}{r} 5.20 \\ -\ 3.87 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Step 2: Subtract from right to left, borrowing when needed.
Hundredths: $0 - 7$ needs a borrow → $10 - 7 = 3$
Tenths: $1 - 8$ needs a borrow → $11 - 8 = 3$
Ones: $4 - 3 = 1$

$$5.2 - 3.87 = 1.33$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always align decimal points, not the last digits.
• Use trailing zeros to make columns match; they do not change the value.
• Check addition by subtracting one number from the answer.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Aligning the last digits instead of the decimal points. For $3.75 + 1.8$, writing $3.75 + 18$ gives $21.75$, which is wrong.

notes.heading: Multiplying and Dividing by Powers of 10
notes.body:
🔑 Key Concept
Multiplying by $10$, $100$ or $1000$ moves every digit one, two or three places to the left, so the decimal point appears to move to the right. Dividing moves digits the other way.

$$\times 10 \rightarrow \text{move decimal point 1 place right}$$
$$\times 100 \rightarrow \text{move decimal point 2 places right}$$
$$\times 1000 \rightarrow \text{move decimal point 3 places right}$$

For division, move the decimal point to the left the same number of places.

💡 Worked Example
Calculate:
(a) $4.73 \times 100$
(b) $6.5 \div 1000$

(a) $4.73 \times 100$: move the decimal point two places right.
$$4.73 \times 100 = 473$$

(b) $6.5 \div 1000$: move the decimal point three places left, adding zeros as needed.
$$6.5 \div 1000 = 0.0065$$

✅ Check
Use estimation to sense-check. $4.73 \times 100$ should be a bit less than $5 \times 100 = 500$, and $473$ fits. $6.5 \div 1000$ should be much smaller than $6.5$, and $0.0065$ is.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Counting the wrong number of zeros. $100$ has two zeros, so move two places; $1000$ has three zeros, so move three places.

notes.heading: Multiplying Two Decimals
notes.body:
🔑 How it works
To multiply two decimals, ignore the decimal points at first. Multiply the numbers as if they were whole numbers. Then count the total number of decimal places in the original factors and place the decimal point in the answer so it has the same total.

💡 Worked Example
Find $2.4 \times 1.35$.

Step 1: Ignore decimals and multiply as whole numbers.
$$24 \times 135 = 3240$$

Step 2: Count decimal places in the original factors.
$2.4$ has $1$ decimal place.
$1.35$ has $2$ decimal places.
Total = $1 + 2 = 3$ decimal places.

Step 3: Place the decimal point in $3240$ to give 3 decimal places.
$$2.4 \times 1.35 = 3.240 = 3.24$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Count decimal places in the question, not the digits.
• Trailing zeros after the decimal point can be removed if they are not needed ($3.240 = 3.24$).
• Estimate first: $2.4 \times 1.35$ is about $2.5 \times 1.3 = 3.25$, so $3.24$ looks right.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting that $2.4 \times 1.35$ must be smaller than $2.4 \times 2 = 4.8$ but larger than $2.4 \times 1 = 2.4$. A quick estimate catches many errors.

notes.heading: Dividing Decimals
notes.body:
🔑 How it works
The easiest way to divide by a decimal is to turn the divisor into a whole number by multiplying both numbers by the same power of 10. Then divide as usual.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Dividing by a decimal
Find $7.2 \div 0.9$.

Step 1: Make the divisor a whole number.
Multiply both numbers by $10$:
$$7.2 \times 10 = 72, \qquad 0.9 \times 10 = 9$$

Step 2: Divide.
$$72 \div 9 = 8$$

So $7.2 \div 0.9 = 8$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — Decimal dividend and divisor
Find $4.68 \div 0.12$.

Step 1: Multiply both by $100$ to make the divisor whole.
$$4.68 \times 100 = 468, \qquad 0.12 \times 100 = 12$$

Step 2: Divide.
$$468 \div 12 = 39$$

So $4.68 \div 0.12 = 39$.

✅ Tip
Check your answer by multiplying back: $0.9 \times 8 = 7.2$ ✓ and $0.12 \times 39 = 4.68$ ✓.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Only multiplying the divisor and forgetting to multiply the dividend by the same amount. If you change one number, you must change the other by the same factor to keep the answer the same.

notes.heading: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Fractions, decimals and percentages are three different ways to represent parts of a whole. They are interchangeable, and being able to convert between them is essential in everyday maths and science.

🔑 Key Concept
• Fraction → decimal: divide numerator by denominator.
• Decimal → percentage: multiply by $100$ and write the % sign.
• Percentage → decimal: divide by $100$ (or move decimal point two places left).
• Decimal → fraction: write the digits over the correct power of 10, then simplify.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Fraction to decimal
Convert $\dfrac{3}{8}$ to a decimal.

$$3 \div 8 = 0.375$$

So $\dfrac{3}{8} = 0.375$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — Decimal to percentage and fraction
Convert $0.64$ to a percentage and a fraction.

Percentage: $0.64 \times 100 = 64\%$
Fraction: $0.64 = \dfrac{64}{100} = \dfrac{16}{25}$

💡 Worked Example 3 — Percentage to decimal
Convert $7.5\%$ to a decimal.

$$7.5\% = 7.5 \div 100 = 0.075$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Common equivalences worth memorising:
  $\dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5 = 50\%$
  $\dfrac{1}{4} = 0.25 = 25\%$
  $\dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75 = 75\%$
  $\dfrac{1}{5} = 0.2 = 20\%$
  $\dfrac{1}{10} = 0.1 = 10\%$
  $\dfrac{1}{100} = 0.01 = 1\%$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Moving the decimal point the wrong way when converting percentages. To go from % to decimal, divide by 100, so $5\% = 0.05$, not $0.5$.

flashcards.definition: The first decimal place; one part out of ten equal parts.
flashcards.example: In 0.4, the digit 4 represents 4 tenths, or 4/10.

flashcards.definition: The second decimal place; one part out of one hundred equal parts.
flashcards.example: In 0.07, the digit 7 represents 7 hundredths, or 7/100.

flashcards.definition: The third decimal place; one part out of one thousand equal parts.
flashcards.example: In 0.009, the digit 9 represents 9 thousandths, or 9/1000.

flashcards.definition: The dot that separates the whole-number part of a number from its fractional part.
flashcards.example: In 12.34, the decimal point separates 12 ones from 34 hundredths.

flashcards.definition: Decimals that represent the same value even though they look different.
Line up the decimal points, add trailing zeros, then compare digits from left to right.
Move every digit left; the decimal point appears to move right by the number of zeros.
Move every digit right; the decimal point appears to move left by the number of zeros.
Align the decimal points and use trailing zeros so the columns match.
Multiply as whole numbers, then count the total decimal places in the factors to place the point.
Multiply both the dividend and divisor by the same power of 10 to make the divisor a whole number.
Divide by 100 (or move the decimal point two places left) and remove the % sign.

questions.stem: In the number 6.295, what is the value of the digit 9?
questions.explanation: After the decimal point, the first digit is tenths, the second is hundredths and the third is thousandths. The 9 is the second digit, so it represents 9 hundredths.
Write 0.4 as 0.40. Since 40 hundredths is greater than 39 hundredths, 0.4 > 0.39.

questions.stem: Which list shows 0.7, 0.08, 0.15 and 0.603 in order from smallest to largest?
questions.explanation: With three decimal places the numbers are 0.700, 0.080, 0.150 and 0.603. Ordering gives 0.080, 0.150, 0.603, 0.700.
Align the decimal points and add: 2.46 + 3.80 = 6.26.
Multiplying by 1000 moves the decimal point three places to the right: 0.058 → 58.
Dividing by 1000 moves the decimal point three places to the left: 34 → 0.034.
6 × 15 = 90. The factors have 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places in total, so the answer is 0.090 = 0.09.
Multiply both numbers by 10 to get 56 ÷ 7 = 8.
7 ÷ 20 = 0.35, or multiply numerator and denominator by 5 to get 35/100 = 0.35.
Multiply by 100 and attach a % sign: 0.065 × 100 = 6.5%.

questions.stem: A backpack costs £32. In a sale it is reduced by 25%. What is the sale price?
Alex buys a drink for £1.85 and a snack for £2.45. He pays with a £10 note. How much change should he receive?
A relay team runs four legs of 1.25 km, 1.8 km, 0.95 km and 2.05 km. What is the total distance?
questions.explanation: Add the distances with decimal points aligned: 1.25 + 1.80 + 0.95 + 2.05 = 6.05 km.

questions.stem: A piece of ribbon 4.5 m long is cut into pieces each 0.75 m long. How many pieces are there?
questions.explanation: Multiply both numbers by 100 to make the divisor whole: 450 ÷ 75 = 6 pieces.
